clue.text: Act altruistically but lose control

definitions.meaning: to put others first and disregard your own interests entirely
to behave rashly, letting temper or emotion take over

explanation.surface: A puzzle about someone whose kindness tips over into a loss of composure.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase has two senses: setting aside self-interest, and losing self-restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means both to be unselfish and to lapse from proper behaviour, two opposite-feeling senses of one phrase.

clue.text: When farewells are said to be in progress

definitions.meaning: split as two words, the phrase means at the point of departure
continuing, still happening

explanation.surface: A remark about goodbyes that seem to drag on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, ON GOING means at the moment of leaving; as one word it means continuing. 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something underway and not yet finished is described as continuing or current.

clue.text: Outfit changed on inclination

definitions.meaning: clothing or kit, as in sports kit
a driver going up a slope shifts to a lower one of these in the car

explanation.surface: Someone swaps their clothes on a whim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inclination' looks like whim or preference, but it is a hill: drivers change down on a gradient. 'Outfit' is the plain sense, kit or clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Kit or equipment is a synonym for clothing, and in a car the cogs you select are shifted on a slope.

clue.text: Young creature to plead insanity

indicators.note: insanity is madness, so the letters of the preceding words go crazy and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A youngster in court pleads not guilty by reason of madness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'insanity' turns the seven letters of TO PLEAD into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A frog's larva is a juvenile animal, a young form of the amphibian.

clue.text: Doctor is upset in row that's offensive

indicators.note: in places the turned doctor inside the row

parts.note: a row is a loud din or racket

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the doctor's letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: MO is medical officer, a common abbreviation for a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor is annoyed by an unpleasant quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a line of seats or a quarrel; it is a din. 'upset' turns the doctor over (a down clue), and 'that's' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Noxious or disgusting things are unpleasant, usually smells; the word has nothing to do with loudness.

clue.text: It may run out in time

definitions.text: It may run out in time

parts.words: It may run out in time
parts.note: think of the grains trickling through an hourglass as it measures time

explanation.surface: A deadline that might be missed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run out' suggests a deadline expiring; it is the grains flowing out of an egg-timer.
explanation.definitionFit: An hourglass measures time by fine grains flowing from one bulb to the other.

clue.text: The rest of one's days

parts.note: rest here means relaxation, not remainder: free time away from work

explanation.surface: The remainder of someone's life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rest' looks like the remainder of a lifetime; it means repose, time off.
explanation.definitionFit: Free time spent relaxing is the restful part of one's days.

clue.text: There's no real alternative to this selection

definitions.text: There's no real alternative to this selection

parts.words: There's no real alternative to this selection
parts.note: a choice that is no choice at all, from a stable keeper who offered only the horse nearest the door

explanation.surface: A complaint that only one option is on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom comes from Thomas Hobson, a Cambridge livery-stable owner who let customers take the horse nearest the door or none.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a take-it-or-leave-it offer where the only option is the one given.

clue.text: Tolerant gathering

definitions.meaning: sympathetic and forgiving of others
as in 'I gather', meaning inferring or grasping what is meant

explanation.surface: A broad-minded meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathering' looks like a meeting; it is the sense of gathering information, grasping it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sympathetic person is forgiving; and comprehension is what you gain when you gather a meaning.

clue.text: Wreck aground despite exercising caution

indicators.note: to wreck is to smash up, so the letters of the next word are broken and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A ship runs aground even though the crew were being careful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wreck' rearranges AGROUND; 'despite' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being watchful and alert against attack is the fencing-derived sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Local board of trade?

parts.note: local is British slang for a neighbourhood pub, and the board advertising it hangs outside

explanation.surface: A council committee overseeing commerce in the area.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is a British pub; its painted board advertises the trade within. 'Board of Trade' was a UK government department.
explanation.definitionFit: The painted signboard hung outside a pub announces its name and business.

clue.text: Error found in a galley-proof

definitions.meaning: a small mistake, as in a ... of the tongue
a printer's long strip of proof

explanation.surface: A misprint spotted while checking printer's proofs.
explanation.walkthrough: In printing, a galley proof is also called a slip; 'found in a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor mistake is a blunder, and printers call a long trial sheet of type by the same name.

clue.text: One offering academic alternative

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A scholar proposes another option.
explanation.definitionFit: A giver who contributes something, such as blood or money, is a contributor.

clue.text: The temptation of misrule

annotationWithheld.why: 'The temptation of misrule (4)': the wordplay is RULE rearranged, signalled by the prefix 'mis' inside the single word 'misrule', which supplies both fodder and indicator in one word

clue.text: It may be drawn or sucked up

definitions.meaning: drawing lots with these stalks, the short one losing
a tube through which a drink is sipped

explanation.surface: Something pulled out or sipped through.
explanation.walkthrough: Two senses: drawing lots, and a drinking tube; 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lots are cast by pulling stalks, and a drinking tube for sipping has the same name.

clue.text: Recreation wear

definitions.meaning: a game or physical pastime
to display or wear proudly

explanation.surface: Casual clothes for leisure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wear' looks like clothing; it is the verb, as in 'sport a beard'.
explanation.definitionFit: Games are a pastime, and to show off a garment or feature is to display it.

clue.text: Close match in which one retires

parts.note: nigh means near
a tie is a cup match or game

explanation.surface: A tight game in which a player has to withdraw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retires' looks like quitting a match; it means going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments worn to bed are what someone puts on when going to sleep.

clue.text: Push former wife in front of train?

indicators.note: in front of puts the former wife ahead of the push in the across entry

parts.note: ex is a former spouse
to press is to push

explanation.surface: A sinister scene of someone shoving an ex-spouse onto the railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in front of train' paints a dark scene, but 'train' is the definition and 'in front of' orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast service making few stops is a type of rail service.

clue.text: Bottle company prompt coming about midday

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the prompt goes round the middle letter

parts.note: to urge is to prompt or encourage
the middle letter of the word day

explanation.surface: A bottling firm reminds staff around noon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' is British slang for nerve. 'coming about' puts URGE round A, the middle of 'day'.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang bottle means nerve or bravery.

clue.text: Girl has the goods, but doesn't seem to know it

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
ware means goods for sale, as in kitchenware

explanation.surface: A woman with all the right attributes is oblivious to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link word. 'the goods' sounds like attractive qualities; it is merchandise.
explanation.definitionFit: Being oblivious means being ignorant of something.

clue.text: It could make me a lord

definitions.text: It could make me a lord

indicators.note: the letters could be formed into something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone dreams of a title elevating them to the peerage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' rearranges ME A LORD; and the whole clue describes what such a title would do.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank and lands of a nobleman confer a title on the holder, making him a peer.

clue.text: Major acting role in Shaw play

definitions.text: Major acting role in Shaw play

parts.words: Major acting role in Shaw play
parts.note: Major is a Salvation Army rank in the title of the Shaw play about Major Undershaft's daughter

explanation.surface: A leading part in a George Bernard Shaw drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Major' looks like 'big'; it is her Salvation Army rank in the title 'Major Barbara'.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of Shaw's play is a Salvation Army officer whose rank and name form its title.

clue.text: One of the party windbags?

parts.note: windbags here are literal bags of air at a party, not boastful politicians

explanation.surface: A dig at a long-winded member of a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party windbags' suggests talkative politicians; it is an inflated decoration at a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflated rubber bag is a party decoration, literally a bag full of wind.

clue.text: Fast scoring rate

definitions.meaning: quick and lively
a tempo marking written on a musical score

explanation.surface: A batsman's quick rate of scoring runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoring' suggests cricket runs; it is a musical score, with the marking as the tempo.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian musical direction means lively and brisk, a tempo written into the score.

clue.text: Like a rugby ball used by cricketers

definitions.meaning: egg-shaped
the London Test cricket ground in Kennington

explanation.surface: A ball shaped for rugby being used in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground where Test matches are played.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg-shaped describes a rugby ball, and a famous London cricket ground has the same name.

clue.text: Medical man badly needed for dental surgery

parts.note: Dr is short for doctor
ill can mean badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: A sick doctor is urgently required at the dentist's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surgery' here is the British word for a dentist's practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A dentist's boring tool is a necessary instrument in a surgery.

clue.text: Hurriedly left without having eaten

annotationWithheld.why: 'Hurriedly left without having eaten (4)': FED around L only works if 'left' gives L while also completing the definition 'Hurriedly left', a word doing two jobs

clue.text: Find this big lake up country

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland

explanation.surface: Find the large lake in the north of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses EIRE; 'Find this' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: One of North America's Great Lakes, it lies between the US and Canada.

clue.text: Let it be in print one sort of square inside another

indicators.note: inside places the first square within the second

parts.note: a set square is another kind of drawing triangle
a T-square is a draughtsman's ruler

explanation.surface: A printer's instruction about geometry tools nesting within each other.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces come from draughting tools: T (T-square) placed inside SET (set square).
explanation.definitionFit: The proofreader's Latin mark tells the printer to ignore a correction and keep the original.

clue.text: Took the meeting and was carried off in triumph

definitions.meaning: presided over a meeting
hoisted shoulder-high by supporters

explanation.surface: A leader ran the meeting and was then lifted aloft by admirers.
explanation.walkthrough: Two senses: presided over, and carried aloft by a crowd; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Presiding over a meeting, and being lifted shoulder-high by a crowd, share the same verb.

clue.text: In a scramble, can go to this figure

indicators.note: a scramble is a jumble, so the words that follow are mixed up

explanation.surface: Advice to rush towards some shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a scramble' rearranges CAN GO TO; 'this' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An eight-sided plane shape is a geometric figure.

clue.text: Resolve to prohibit race on motorway

indicators.note: in an across entry, on means placed after, so the race follows the motorway

parts.note: deter means to discourage or prevent
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI
a nation is a people or race

explanation.surface: A decision to ban racing on a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's London-Leeds motorway; the figure 1 is treated as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Firmness of purpose is resolve as a noun, steadfast will.
